title: Exact Dynamic Programming (Dynp) — Dynp
text: Dynp finds segmentation globally minimises total cost specified number change-points – unlike PELT (exact penalty, change-point count) binSeg (greedy split, guaranteed globally optimal fixed count), Dynp exact whatever nBkps requested. price complexity: building full table costs \(O(\text{nBkpsMax} \cdot M^2)\) \(M\) number (minSize, jump)-admissible grid points (\(M \approx n/\text{jump}\) worst case), versus PELT's near-linear pruning binSeg's \(O(n \log n)\)-ish greedy search. $fit() computes exact minimal cost every change-point count 0 nBkpsMax one pass (see $costPath()). Dynp therefore useful exact fixed-number--change-points solution required, particularly using custom cost functions PELT pruning guaranteed. Dynp requires R6 object class costFunc, exactly PELT/binSeg/Window – see costFunc supported cost functions ("L1", "L2", "SIGMA", "VAR", "LinearL2", "LinearSIGMA", "LinearL1", "Custom"). examples provided . See package website detailed usage!
